title: findings_register.v1
description: The CAPA register: one row per finding in the proof journal (docs/POC_JOURNAL.md), kept at docs/FINDINGS_REGISTER.json. The journal is the immutable record of each finding; the register is its living status: risk ranking, deadline, closure, and verification. Severity rubric: critical = an exploitable security exposure or a control that admits what it must refuse (fix within 7 days); high = a control that silently does not run or checks nothing, or a governance gap that removes a guardrail (30 days); medium = a defect or missing proof with a working control around it (90 days); low = maintainability or reuse (180 days). A row's due date is at most its found date plus its severity's days, checked by tests/journal/register.py, which also fails an overdue open finding on the daily run, computes the control-effectiveness metrics, and reports production readiness: false while any critical or high finding in the security or governance category is open.

controls.description: The gate's control classes, each proven or not: shown to fail on the defect it guards against. The share proven is a control-effectiveness metric.

detected_by.description: control: a check, scanner, or test reported it; person: someone looking found it. Set by hand and not yet verified against evidence: the share recorded as found by controls is reported as an attribution, not as verified detection effectiveness.

status.description: fixed: the correction and preventive action are in place; proven: a designed-to-fail case shows the control catches the defect.

verification.description: Where the proof is: runs, commits, pull requests, reports.

residual.description: What a closed finding still leaves open, stated rather than implied.
